cefr_model.subdivision_notice: The .1 and .2 levels are internal curriculum subdivisions, not official CEFR levels.

concepts.name: Listening
concepts.description: Build meaning from spoken English in progressively wider contexts.

evidence_or_reference.note: Original prototype category aligned broadly to the CEFR language-activity model; no descriptor text is reproduced.

concepts.name: Spoken production
concepts.description: Produce planned or sustained spoken English for a communicative purpose.

evidence_or_reference.note: Original skill label and description informed by the CEFR activity framework without copying descriptors.

concepts.name: Spoken interaction
concepts.description: Take alternating speaker and listener roles to achieve a shared purpose.

evidence_or_reference.note: Original prototype formulation based on the CEFR distinction between production, reception, and interaction.

concepts.name: Reading
concepts.description: Construct meaning from written English for practical, informational, and reflective purposes.

evidence_or_reference.note: Original description attached to an authoritative framework citation.

concepts.name: Written production
concepts.description: Create written English suited to an audience, purpose, and text type.

evidence_or_reference.note: Original description attached to an authoritative framework citation.

concepts.name: Mediation

evidence_or_reference.note: Mediation is retained as a broad framework dimension; this wording and internal placement are project-authored.

concepts.name: Present simple
concepts.description: Use present-tense forms for recurring situations, stable states, and general statements.

evidence_or_reference.note: Project-authored grammar prototype; the citation informs broad CEFR alignment rather than an exact official grammar assignment.

concepts.name: Past simple
concepts.description: Locate completed events or states before the present reference point.

evidence_or_reference.note: Original pedagogical sequencing hypothesis to be independently reviewed before approval.

evidence_or_reference.note: Original cross-dimensional bridge between grammar and discourse.

concepts.name: Past perfect
concepts.description: Mark one past situation as earlier than another relevant past point.

evidence_or_reference.note: Original pedagogical sequencing hypothesis to be independently reviewed before approval.

vocabulary_senses.definition: Move on foot at a pace that is normally faster than walking.
examples: Mai runs to the gate when the rain starts.

evidence_or_reference.note: Definition, combinations, and example are original prototype text; URL retained only as a future lexical cross-check.

vocabulary_senses.definition: Manage or organize an activity, service, or organization.
examples: Lan runs a small language club at the library.

evidence_or_reference.note: Definition, combinations, and example are original prototype text; URL retained only as a future lexical cross-check.

vietnamese_learner_annotations.description: Some Vietnamese learners may reduce English syllable-final consonant clusters; individual performance must be assessed rather than assumed.
vietnamese_learner_annotations.teaching_response: Use perception checks and gradual production practice while avoiding deficit labels or blanket claims about all learners.

evidence_or_reference.note: Paraphrased narrow finding from a case study; evidence is limited and does not justify population-wide prediction.

vietnamese_learner_annotations.description: During review, check article choices explicitly instead of presuming that every Vietnamese learner has the same difficulty.
vietnamese_learner_annotations.teaching_response: Use contextual noticing tasks and record learner-specific evidence before assigning remediation.

evidence_or_reference.note: Project-authored teaching caution, not a research claim and not attributed to the cited framework.
